subject: ILCE-6400 updater receiver, transcode, and body pipeline boundary

receiver.reason: The updater-mode command dispatcher writes each command 0x0040 payload into /tmp_updater/Firm.dat, and command 0x0100 launches crypter.elf on that file; the signed host updater contains only this transfer loop before completion.

observations.source: Static decompilation of libupdaterufp.so and the signed Windows updater transfer loop
observations.claim: Updater command 0x0040 writes the FDAT stream to /tmp_updater/Firm.dat, command 0x0100 launches crypter.elf on that file, and no second host transfer follows.

observations.source: Static decompilation of crypter.elf, libupdatercommon.so, and libupdaterbody.so
observations.claim: crypter.elf constructs an Updater::RingBuffer, its MsDecryptorModule consumes 0x400-byte frames, and the body loader resolves GetBody and ReleaseBody before invoking UpdaterBody::Execute on the produced stream.

observations.source: Static decompilation of libupdatertalk.so and digest comparison with historical updater tooling
observations.claim: Dec_Scramble initializes an AES-128 decryption schedule and independently decrypts 16-byte blocks in ECB mode using the historical first-stage key family; no CBC implementation is present in this library.

observations.source: Static inspection and partial generic Xtensa decoding of sa_aes_sha2.bin and sa_udrt.bin
observations.claim: The secure AES/SHA program is a pointer-mapped Xtensa custom-extension image containing standard AES and SHA-256 tables, while the generic decoder cannot fully decode its custom instructions.

inferences.source: Combined generation-4 FDAT geometry, historical fwtool cipher modes, and the observed crypter AES-ECB consumer
inferences.claim: The generation-4 remainder must be transformed into legacy first-stage ECB ciphertext before crypter.elf consumes it; sending raw CBC ciphertext or CBC plaintext directly to this consumer is inconsistent with the observed second AES decryption.

inferences.source: The single host transfer and the user-space command 0x0040 write callback
inferences.claim: The missing transform must occur at or before data reaches the user-space UFP write path, plausibly in a lower AV or secure execution layer, but the responsible component and call path are not yet established.

unresolved.source: No proven cross-reference from the updater receive path to either secure program
unresolved.claim: The producer, command ABI, key derivation, and exact generation-4 transcode implementation remain unknown, including whether sa_aes_sha2.bin or sa_udrt.bin participates.

unresolved.source: The 0x100-byte FDAT suffix is structurally plausible as a signature but has no located verifier
unresolved.claim: The signature algorithm, verifier implementation, trust anchor, and signed byte range remain unproven.

unresolved.source: No model-compatible donor payload or camera-side execution evidence
unresolved.claim: Decryption and portable integration of newer-camera UI, touch-control, and Creative Look components into the ILCE-6400 remain unproven.

conclusion: The ILCE-6400 updater-mode FDAT receiver, crypter, ring-buffer producer, and body archive consumer are now located. The evidence requires an unresolved generation-4-to-legacy ECB transcode before crypter.elf, while the secure invocation path and firmware signature boundary remain unknown. This report establishes no bypass and produces no installable or model-mismatch-safe image.
